profile.campus: Somerset, Franklin Township, Somerset County, New Jersey (CyrusOne NYM1)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own facility page, NYM1 sits at 800 Cottontail Ln, Somerset, NJ 08873, currently publishing 185,000 sq ft of technical IT space operational and 23 MW of total IT capacity, with a full build-out plan CyrusOne states could reach over 430,000 sq ft; CyrusOne describes the site as a carrier-neutral facility built to Tier III+ topology with N+2 redundancy serving the New York/New Jersey metro market.

Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry states the company acquired Cervalis, a Connecticut-area data center and colocation provider, in July 2015 for approximately $400 million; whether that acquisition specifically included this Somerset, NJ site was not confirmed in sourcing fetched this session, so it is noted as regional-era context rather than a direct acquisition history for NYM1. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, was purchased by Cincinnati Bell for $525 million in 2010, completed an IPO in January 2013, and was taken private when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) closed a roughly $15 billion acquisition in March 2022. This registry also carries a separate mapped point, osm:way/460182320, labeled "CyrusOne Somerset" in the same county; that row's own reverse-geocoded coordinates resolve to a different street (Pierce Street, Franklin Township) than this NYM1 address, so the two are not asserted here as the same facility despite the shared name and county.

In November 2021, KKR and GIP first announced the agreement to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately $15 billion transaction, one of the largest data center M&A deals of that period, reflecting broader private-equity and infrastructure-fund interest in colocation real estate that has also driven acquisitions of peers like QTS (by Blackstone) and CoreSite (by American Tower) around the same era; CyrusOne's current published portfolio language describes more than 50 mission-critical facilities worldwide, though the company's own site and Wikipedia give somewhat different approximate totals (over 40 versus more than 50), neither of which this registry treats as a precise, independently verified figure.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Somerset (NYM1) publishes 23 MW of IT load capacity across 185,000 square feet of operational technical space in Somerset, New Jersey. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, this translates to roughly 575 racks. The facility is built to Tier III+ topology with N+2 redundancy. The operator states a full build-out plan could reach over 430,000 square feet, though no expanded capacity figure is published.

This campus ranks second by published capacity among the five facilities in New Jersey reporting IT megawatts, and represents 21 percent of the 111.3 MW of published capacity across the state. The site sits in the New York and New Jersey metro market and is designated carrier neutral, though no certifications specific to accelerator hosting are published. New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities overall, of which this site is one.

No certifications qualifying the campus for specific workloads are published. The facility's expansion potential and carrier-neutral status indicate it could scale significantly beyond current published capacity, but future power availability and actual tenant allocation are not published. The research session did not locate a specific opening date or investment figure for this facility.
